description: Turn a plain-language claim into proposed Countersign checks, deterministically (URLs, domains, PRs, shas, IPs, quoted text, repo paths; no LLM). Ranked by confidence and by how each recipe has held up in the ledger. Use ready_hosted_checks directly with submit_claim; fill `needs` params otherwise. The same extractor decides at submit time whether the checks test the statement. `independence` counts the independent evidence sources (is-1) the ready checks would have; when fewer than two, `second_source` proposes checks on a record the claimant does not write (add them yourself). `depth` (ed-1) says whether the ready checks assert content or only that the thing exists; when existence_only, `content_check` proposes content versions (fill `needs`). Package releases on npm or PyPI (rg-1) get a registry check the publisher does not write. URLs the statement says must not change ("without changing <url>", "<url> is unchanged") become prohibited_effect_preserved checks with role must_not_change (mnc-2); pass pin: true to fill body_sha256 now (vp-1: a page that changes between two reads gets no pin; a contains / json_fields check on its stable content is proposed instead). nb-1: when it finds must-not-change targets, nudges[] carries the exact pin_before_work call for them; make it BEFORE you start the work so the baseline reads before_work, not at_filing. rp-1: when ready_hosted_checks would pin a value that changes on every release, release_pin (and a string in warnings[]) names each pin so you can drop them before submit_claim.

pin.description: mnc-2: for URLs the statement says must not change, read each body's sha256 now with the checker's own fetch (at most 3) so the prohibited_effect_preserved check is ready to submit

name: suggest_checks
title: Suggest checks for a claim
